tutorial.title: Hanging jar lantern
tutorial.adapted_note: Adapted for Beginner: pliers instead of a drill, no glass cutting.

tools.alternative: A straightened metal coat hanger or a sturdy key-ring chain

safety: Wear work gloves when bending wire
Check the jar for chips before you start

steps.title: Soak off the label
steps.instruction: Fill a bowl with warm soapy water and soak the jar for 10 minutes, then peel the label and rub off the glue with a cloth.
steps.tip: A little cooking oil lifts stubborn glue.
steps.image_prompt: the same jar with the paper label fully removed, clean and dry on the counter, lid set aside

steps.title: Wrap the wire collar
steps.instruction: Wrap craft wire twice around the groove under the rim and twist the ends together with pliers until it doesn't slide.
steps.warning: Wire ends are sharp: tuck them flat against the glass.
steps.image_prompt: the same clean jar with a snug double loop of thin silver wire twisted around the neck under the rim

steps.title: Add the handle
steps.instruction: Cut 30 cm of wire, hook each end through the collar on opposite sides and bend them closed to form an arch.
steps.image_prompt: the same jar now with an arched wire handle attached to the neck collar on both sides

steps.title: Wrap the handle in twine
steps.instruction: Tie twine to one end of the handle and wind it tightly along the arch. Tie off and dab the knot with glue if you have some.
steps.tip: Keep each turn touching the last for a neat finish.
steps.image_prompt: the same jar lantern with its wire handle fully wrapped in natural brown twine

steps.title: Add sand and a tea light
steps.instruction: Pour 2 cm of sand or pebbles into the jar and press a tea light into the middle.
steps.warning: Use an LED tea light indoors and never leave a flame unattended.
steps.image_prompt: the finished jar lantern with a layer of pale sand inside and a tea light sitting in the middle, lit

finishing: Hang it from a hook at least 30 cm below anything that can burn
care: Wipe soot off the inside with a damp cloth
Replace the sand if wax spills into it
